questions.title: Box of Any Type
questions.description:
A moving company stores items of different types in sealed boxes. Write a generic class Box<T> with a constructor and a getter, then create a box of the type named by the input tag and print what it holds.

Input Format:
One line with a tag (int, double or string) followed by one value token.

Output Format:
Print 'Stored value: v' and then 'Type: SimpleName' where v is the stored value and SimpleName is Integer, Double or String.

Constraints:
Numeric values are between -1000000 and 1000000; string values are single tokens of 1 to 20 characters
questions.inputconstrains: tag in {int, double, string}; -1000000 <= numeric value <= 1000000; string tokens 1-20 chars

questions.title: First of Two Generics
questions.description:
Generic methods let one method serve many types without overloading. Implement a generic method declared as public static <T> T first(T a, T b) that always returns its first argument, and call it from main based on the input tag.

Input Format:
One line starting with a tag (int or string) followed by two space-separated values of that type.

Output Format:
Print 'First: v' where v is the first value.

Constraints:
Integers are between -1000000 and 1000000; strings are single tokens of 1 to 20 characters
questions.inputconstrains: tag in {int, string}; integers -1000000 <= v <= 1000000; strings 1-20 chars

questions.title: Generic Pair Printer
questions.description:
A key-value registry needs to hold any combination of key and value types. Define a generic class Pair<K, V> with a two-argument constructor and a toString that returns [key, value], then print the pair built from the input.

Input Format:
One line: ktype vtype kvalue vvalue where ktype and vtype are each int or string, and kvalue and vvalue are matching value tokens.

Output Format:
Print 'Pair: [k, v]'.

Constraints:
Integers are between -1000000 and 1000000; strings are single tokens of 1 to 20 characters
questions.inputconstrains: ktype, vtype in {int, string}; integers -1000000 <= v <= 1000000; strings 1-20 chars

questions.title: Lambda Calculator
questions.description:
Building a tiny calculator is a classic first use of lambdas. Define a functional interface Calc with a method int apply(int a, int b), create lambda instances for +, -, * and /, and dispatch on the input operator.

Input Format:
One line: a op b where op is one of + - * /.

Output Format:
Print the integer result of applying the chosen operation (integer division for /).

Constraints:
-1000000 <= a, b <= 1000000; b is never 0 when op is /

questions.title: Predicate String Checker
questions.description:
Form validation often starts with simple boolean checks. Using java.util.function.Predicate with lambdas, check whether a word starts with the capital letter A and whether its length is at least a given limit, printing both results.

Input Format:
One line: a word token followed by an integer limit.

Output Format:
Print 'Starts with A: b' then 'Length at least L: b' where each b is true or false in lowercase.

Constraints:
The word has 1 to 20 letters; 1 <= limit <= 25
questions.sampleoutput1:
Starts with A: true
Length at least 3: true
questions.sampleoutput2:
Starts with A: false
Length at least 10: false
questions.output1:
Starts with A: true
Length at least 5: false
questions.output2:
Starts with A: false
Length at least 3: true
questions.output3:
Starts with A: true
Length at least 7: true

questions.title: Function Mapper
questions.description:
A math helper app maps one number to another through simple transforms. Using java.util.function.Function with lambdas, apply the operation named in the input to the given number.

Input Format:
One line: an integer n followed by an operation token (double, square or negate).

Output Format:
Print the transformed value: n*2 for double, n*n for square, -n for negate.

Constraints:
-1000 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Cart Total with Tax
questions.description:
An online store checkout adds sales tax as the very last step. Represent that tax step as a Function<Double, Double> lambda that takes the base price and returns the price with tax added, then print the final total.

Input Format:
One line: base price and tax rate percent, both decimals.

Output Format:
Print the total with exactly 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= price <= 100000; 0 <= rate <= 50

questions.title: Credential Validator
questions.description:
A login service checks credentials with two rules before granting access. Using Predicate lambdas, verify that the username has at least 4 characters and the password has at least 6 characters, and grant access only when both rules pass.

Input Format:
One line: a username token and a password token.

Output Format:
Print 'Access granted' if both checks pass, otherwise 'Access denied'.

Constraints:
Username and password are single tokens of 1 to 20 characters
questions.inputconstrains: username and password are single tokens of 1-20 characters

questions.title: Temperature Converter Suite
questions.description:
A weather dashboard converts temperatures between scales. Build the three converters as Function<Double, Double> lambdas (c2f: v*9/5+32, f2c: (v-32)*5/9, k2c: v-273.15) and apply the one named in the input.

Input Format:
One line: a decimal value and a mode (c2f, f2c or k2c).

Output Format:
Print the converted value with exactly 2 decimals.

Constraints:
-1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Library Catalog Lookup
questions.description:
A library shelf tracks how many copies of each book are present. Model each shelf entry with your generic class Pair<K, V> (here Pair<String, Integer>) with getKey and getValue accessors, store the entries in a list, then print the catalog in input order.

Input Format:
The first token is n. Each of the next n pairs is a call number token followed by an integer copy count.

Output Format:
For each entry print 'call -> copies' on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10; call numbers are 1 to 10 characters; 0 <= copies <= 100
